sourceOccurrences.label: Offspring generating functions and their least fixed point
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Source-inspected exposition with explicit scope distinctions
sourceOccurrences.note: The source proves the analytic content of 8TFY and BFM4 for an arbitrary probability mass function on the natural numbers, including infinite mean and the deterministic one-child exception. Identifying the iterates with generation extinction probabilities requires a separate process construction.

sourceOccurrences.label: Square-root Laplace deficits and tail bounds
sourceOccurrences.note: Fourteen public results give the analytic MIFH implication with extended natural volumes and a nontrivial generating-function witness. No exact tail equivalent or local limit is asserted. Source pin: 3978a2fa0ec425729f6e15fbc3c6a142cfa4a672.

sourceOccurrences.label: Critical offspring transforms
sourceOccurrences.note: Seventeen public results prove the second-order expansion, unique transform root and its square-root asymptotic. A finite second factorial moment suffices; identification with a progeny law is separate. Source pin: 3978a2fa0ec425729f6e15fbc3c6a142cfa4a672.

sourceOccurrences.label: Quadratic survival and Yaglom recursions
sourceOccurrences.note: Seven public results prove the reciprocal-increment and fixed-lambda array limits with their uniformity hypotheses explicit. Source pin: 3978a2fa0ec425729f6e15fbc3c6a142cfa4a672.

proofUses.reason: Root decomposition and the critical fixed-point criterion, with the uniform generating-function expansion proved in N9P5; the new comparison permits either sign of the mean displacement.
The finite-variance generating-function recursion and the survival asymptotic give the conditional Laplace limit; exact generation means supply uniform integrability.

Dwass reduces progeny probabilities to a central lattice coefficient, computed directly by Fourier inversion under finite positive variance. Critical extinction justifies the concluding tail comparison; the local proof does not use a Tauberian implication.
The equal-time correspondence controls distortion, roots and the coupled mass measures. Edge-to-child coupling compares contour occupation with uniform vertex mass.

The conditioned-contour invariance theorem is an explicit external input. LHWC gives measured-tree convergence and continuity gives height/diameter. NOKH identifies admissible sizes; NT0R supplies the uniform ordered-tree specialization.
